facts.raw_span: a 1½-week history of headache and blurred vision
MRI of the brain demonstrated a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
an HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL
Serum toxoplasma IgG was elevated
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes) with positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii (286 copies/mL)
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
fever to 39.6 °C
generalized weakness
a 1-day history of productive cough
Chest radiograph showed a new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence
CT scan of the chest confirmed extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates with focal consolidation in the left upper lobe

concepts.why: The patient has a ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect, elevated serum toxoplasma IgG, and positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF studies, which are all consistent with toxoplasmosis.

The patient has a new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence, extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates with focal consolidation in the left upper lobe, and a low CD4 count, which are all consistent with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
The patient has a CD4 count <20 cells/µL and an HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL, which indicates severe immunosuppression.

The patient has a ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect, elevated serum toxoplasma IgG, and positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF studies, which are all consistent with cerebral toxoplasmosis.
The patient has a CD4 count <20 cells/µL and an HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL, which indicates severe immunosuppression and meets the criteria for AIDS.

The patient has a new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence, extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates with focal consolidation in the left upper lobe, and worsening respiratory status, which are all consistent with respiratory failure.
The patient has a low CD4 count and multiple opportunistic infections, including toxoplasmosis and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, which are all consistent with opportunistic infection.
The patient has a CD4 count <20 cells/µL and an HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL, which indicates severe immunosuppression and an immunocompromised state.

rationales.F03: Severe immunosuppression increases the risk of opportunistic infections, including toxoplasmosis and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
rationales.F05: Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG is a strong indicator of toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F06: Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF confirm the diagnosis of cerebral toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F07: Presence of bradyzoites and tachyzoites in brain tissue is diagnostic of toxoplasmosis.
